title: "C Loops"
---

## Description

This is the third notebook. It introduces repetition in C through the `while`, `for`, and `do while` loops, then covers `break`, `continue`, and `return`, classic loop problems such as Fibonacci numbers and patterns, menus that repeat, and finally small games that loop until the player wins or loses.

## How to use the pack

Work through the exercises in order, since later ones build on earlier ones. Attempt the Questions before revealing the answer. If a solution is unclear, ask LLMs for a step-by-step explanation.

## Part 1 — The `while` Loop

A `while` loop checks its condition **before** every repetition. Make sure something inside the loop eventually makes the condition false.

### 1. Count from 1 to 5
**Question:** Use a `while` loop to print the numbers `1` through `5`, each on its own line.

**Expected Output:**
```text
1
2
3
4
5
```

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show answer"}
```c
#include <stdio.h>

int main() {
    int i = 1;
    while (i <= 5) {
        printf("%d\n", i);
        i++;
    }
    return 0;
}
```
The counter `i` starts at `1`, and `i++` moves it toward the end. Forgetting `i++` would create an infinite loop.
:::

### 2. A Loop That Never Runs
**Question:** Predict the output.

**The Code:**
```c
#include <stdio.h>

int main() {
    int i = 10;
    while (i < 5) {
        printf("%d\n", i);
        i++;
    }
    printf("done\n");
    return 0;
}
```

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show answer"}
**Output:**
```text
done
```
The condition `10 < 5` is false from the start, so the loop body never runs.
:::

### 3. Trace a `while` Loop
**Question:** Predict the output. Track both variables after every repetition.

**The Code:**
```c
#include <stdio.h>

int main() {
    int i = 1, total = 0;
    while (i <= 4) {
        total += i;
        i++;
    }
    printf("%d %d\n", i, total);
    return 0;
}
```

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show answer"}
**Output:**
```text
5 10
```
`total` becomes `1`, `3`, `6`, then `10`. The loop stops when `i` reaches `5`, so `i` is `5` after the loop, one more than the last value that was added.
:::

### 4. Sum from 1 to N
**Question:** Read a positive integer `N`. Use a loop to calculate `1 + 2 + ... + N` and print the sum. Assume the result fits in an `int`.

**Expected Program Output** (Input: 4)**:** 
```text
Enter a positive integer: 4
Sum: 10
```

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show answer"}
```c
#include <stdio.h>

int main() {
    int n, i = 1;
    int sum = 0;
    printf("Enter a positive integer: ");
    scanf("%d", &n);
    printf("\n");

    while (i <= n) {
        sum += i;
        i++;
    }
    printf("Sum: %d\n", sum);
    return 0;
}
```
`sum` must start at `0` before the loop. This pattern of building up a total is called an accumulator.
:::

### 5. Sum Until the User Enters 0
**Question:** Keep reading integers and adding them. Stop when the user enters `0`, and do not add the zero. Print the final sum. Assume the user enters at least one number before the `0`.

**Expected Program Output:**<br>
Input: 5, 3, 0
```text
Enter a number (0 to stop): 5
Enter a number (0 to stop): 3
Enter a number (0 to stop): 0
Sum: 8
```

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show answer"}
```c
#include <stdio.h>

int main() {
    int number;
    int sum = 0;
    printf("Enter a number (0 to stop): ");
    scanf("%d", &number);
    printf("\n");

    while (number != 0) {
        sum += number;
        printf("Enter a number (0 to stop): ");
        scanf("%d", &number);
        printf("\n");
    }
    printf("Sum: %d\n", sum);
    return 0;
}
```
The first number is read before the loop so the condition has a value to check. The next number is read at the end of each repetition. A stopping value like `0` is called a sentinel.
:::

### 6. Count the Digits (Optional)
**Question:** Read a positive integer and print how many digits it has. Repeatedly divide it by `10`.

**Expected Program Output** (Input: 4096)**:**
```text
Enter a positive integer: 4096
Digits: 4
```

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show answer"}
```c
#include <stdio.h>

int main() {
    int n, count = 0;
    printf("Enter a positive integer: ");
    scanf("%d", &n);
    printf("\n");

    while (n > 0) {
        n /= 10;
        count++;
    }
    printf("Digits: %d\n", count);
    return 0;
}
```
Integer division by `10` removes the last digit: `4096` becomes `409`, `40`, `4`, and finally `0`.
:::

## Part 2 — The `for` Loop

A `for` loop puts the three parts of a counting loop in one line: `for (start; condition; update)`.

### 7. Count Down (Optional)
**Question:** Use a `for` loop to print `5`, `4`, `3`, `2`, `1` on separate lines, then print `Go!`.

**Expected Output:**
```text
5
4
3
2
1
Go!
```

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show answer"}
```c
#include <stdio.h>

int main() {
    for (int i = 5; i >= 1; i--) {
        printf("%d\n", i);
    }
    printf("Go!\n");
    return 0;
}
```
:::

### 8. Step Size
**Question:** Predict the output.

**The Code:**
```c
#include <stdio.h>

int main() {
    for (int i = 0; i < 10; i += 3) {
        printf("%d\n", i);
    }
    return 0;
}
```

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show answer"}
**Output:**
```text
0
3
6
9
```
The update part can be any change, here `i += 3`. After `9`, the next value is `12`, which fails `i < 10`.
:::

### 9. Sum a Chosen Number of Inputs
**Question:** First read how many numbers the user will enter, then read exactly that many integers, add them, and print the total. Assume the count is at least `1`. Do not use an array.

**Expected Program Output:**<br>
Input: 3, 4, 10, -2
```text
How many numbers? 3
Number 1: 4
Number 2: 10
Number 3: -2
Total: 12
```

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show answer"}
```c
#include <stdio.h>

int main() {
    int count, number;
    int sum = 0;
    printf("How many numbers? ");
    scanf("%d", &count);
    printf("\n");

    for (int i = 1; i <= count; i++) {
        printf("Number %d: ", i);
        scanf("%d", &number);
        printf("\n");
        sum += number;
    }
    printf("Total: %d\n", sum);
    return 0;
}
```
Use `for` when you know in advance how many repetitions you need.
:::

### 10. Multiplication Table
**Question:** Read an integer and print its multiplication table from `number x 1` through `number x 10`.

**Expected Program Output** (Input: 7)**:**
```text
Enter an integer: 7
7 x 1 = 7
7 x 2 = 14
7 x 3 = 21
7 x 4 = 28
7 x 5 = 35
7 x 6 = 42
7 x 7 = 49
7 x 8 = 56
7 x 9 = 63
7 x 10 = 70
```

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show answer"}
```c
#include <stdio.h>

int main() {
    int number;
    printf("Enter an integer: ");
    scanf("%d", &number);
    printf("\n");

    for (int i = 1; i <= 10; i++) {
        printf("%d x %d = %d\n", number, i, number * i);
    }

}
```
:::

### 11. Factorial
**Question:** Read an integer `n` from `0` to `12` and print `n!`. Remember that `0!` is `1`. For any other input, print `Invalid input`.

**Expected Program Output** (Input: 5)**:**
```text
Enter n (0-12): 5
5! = 120
```

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show answer"}
```c
#include <stdio.h>

int main() {
    int n;
    int result = 1;
    printf("Enter n (0-12): ");
    scanf("%d", &n);
    printf("\n");

    if (n < 0 || n > 12) {
        printf("Invalid input\n");
        return 0;
    }
    for (int i = 1; i <= n; i++) {
        result *= i;
    }
    printf("%d! = %d\n", n, result);
    return 0;
}
```
`result` starts at `1` (not `0`), because it is multiplied each time. The loop does not run for `n = 0`, so the result stays `1`. Above `12!`, the value no longer fits in an `int`.
:::

### 12. Even Numbers up to N
**Question:** Read `N` and print all even numbers from `2` up to `N` on one line, separated by single spaces. Use a step of `2` in the `for` loop.

**Expected Program Output** (Input: 10)**:**
```text
Enter N: 10
2 4 6 8 10
```

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show answer"}
```c
#include <stdio.h>

int main() {
    int n;
    printf("Enter N: ");
    scanf("%d", &n);
    printf("\n");

    for (int i = 2; i <= n; i += 2) {
        if (i > 2) {
            printf(" ");
        }
        printf("%d", i);
    }
    printf("\n");
    return 0;
}
```
The space is printed before every number except the first, so there is no extra space at the end of the line.
:::

### 13. Largest of a Chosen Number of Inputs (Optional)
**Question:** Read how many numbers will be entered, then read that many integers and print the largest. Assume the count is at least `1`. Do not use an array. Keep the largest value seen so far in one variable.

**Expected Program Output:**<br>
Input: 4, 7, -3, 12, 9
```text
How many numbers? 4
Enter number 1: 7
Enter number 2: -3
Enter number 3: 12
Enter number 4: 9
Largest: 12
```

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show answer"}
```c
#include <stdio.h>

int main() {
    int count, number, largest;
    printf("How many numbers? ");
    scanf("%d", &count);
    printf("\n");

    printf("Enter number 1: ");
    scanf("%d", &largest);
    printf("\n");
    for (int i = 2; i <= count; i++) {
        printf("Enter number %d: ", i);
        scanf("%d", &number);
        printf("\n");
        if (number > largest) {
            largest = number;
        }
    }
    printf("Largest: %d\n", largest);
    return 0;
}
```
Starting `largest` with the first input (instead of `0`) also works for negative numbers.
:::

## Part 3 — The `do while` Loop

A `do while` loop checks its condition **after** the body, so the body always runs at least once.

### 14. A Loop That Runs Once
**Question:** Predict the output. Compare this with Question 2.

**The Code:**
```c
#include <stdio.h>

int main() {
    int i = 10;
    do {
        printf("%d\n", i);
        i++;
    } while (i < 5);
    return 0;
}
```

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show answer"}
**Output:**
```text
10
```
The body runs once before the condition `11 < 5` is checked. The condition is false, so the loop ends.
:::

### 15. Validate a Menu Choice
**Question:** Keep asking the user for a number from `1` to `3` until the input is valid, then print `Accepted`.

**Expected Program Output:**<br>
Input: 7, 0, 2
```text
Enter a choice from 1 to 3: 7
Enter a choice from 1 to 3: 0
Enter a choice from 1 to 3: 2
Accepted
```

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show answer"}
```c
#include <stdio.h>

int main() {
    int choice;
    do {
        printf("Enter a choice from 1 to 3: ");
        scanf("%d", &choice);
        printf("\n");
    } while (choice < 1 || choice > 3);

    printf("Accepted\n");
    return 0;
}
```
`do while` fits here because the program must ask at least once before it can check the answer.
:::

## Part 4 — `break`, `continue`, and `return`

- `break` leaves the **loop** immediately.
- `continue` skips the rest of the current repetition and goes to the next one.
- `return` leaves the whole **function**. In `main`, that ends the program.

### 16. `break` Leaves the Loop
**Question:** Predict the output.

**The Code:**
```c
#include <stdio.h>

int main() {
    for (int i = 1; i <= 10; i++) {
        if (i == 4) {
            break;
        }
        printf("%d\n", i);
    }
    printf("after\n");
    return 0;
}
```

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show answer"}
**Output:**
```text
1
2
3
after
```
When `i` is `4`, `break` ends the loop. The program continues with the statement after the loop.
:::

### 17. `continue` Skips One Repetition
**Question:** Predict the output.

**The Code:**
```c
#include <stdio.h>

int main() {
    for (int i = 1; i <= 6; i++) {
        if (i % 2 == 0) {
            continue;
        }
        printf("%d\n", i);
    }
    return 0;
}
```

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show answer"}
**Output:**
```text
1
3
5
```
For even values of `i`, `continue` jumps straight to the next repetition, so `printf` is skipped. The `i++` in the `for` header still runs.
:::

### 18. `break` and `continue` Together (Optional)
**Question:** Predict the output, including the value of `i` after the loop.

**The Code:**
```c
#include <stdio.h>

int main() {
    int i;
    for (i = 1; i <= 8; i++) {
        if (i == 3) {
            continue;
        }
        if (i == 5) {
            break;
        }
        printf("%d\n", i);
    }
    printf("i = %d\n", i);
    return 0;
}
```

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show answer"}
**Output:**
```text
1
2
4
i = 5
```
`3` is skipped by `continue`. At `5`, `break` ends the loop before `i++` runs, so `i` keeps the value `5`. The variable `i` is declared before the loop so it can be printed afterwards.
:::

### 19. `return` Inside a Loop
**Question:** Predict the output. Does `done` print?

**The Code:**
```c
#include <stdio.h>

int main() {
    for (int i = 1; i <= 5; i++) {
        printf("%d\n", i);
        if (i == 3) {
            return 0;
        }
    }
    printf("done\n");
    return 0;
}
```

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show answer"}
**Output:**
```text
1
2
3
```
`return 0;` ends `main`, and therefore the whole program, so `done` never prints. A `break` in the same place would have printed `done`.
:::

### 20. Infinite Loop with an Exit
**Question:** Use `while (1)` to read integers until the user enters a negative number. Add up the non-negative numbers and print the sum. Use `break` to leave the loop.

**Expected Program Output:**<br>
Input: 5, 3, -1
```text
Enter a number (negative to stop): 5
Enter a number (negative to stop): 3
Enter a number (negative to stop): -1
Sum: 8
```

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show answer"}
```c
#include <stdio.h>

int main() {
    int number;
    int sum = 0;

    while (1) {
        printf("Enter a number (negative to stop): ");
        scanf("%d", &number);
        printf("\n");
        if (number < 0) {
            break;
        }
        sum += number;
    }
    printf("Sum: %d\n", sum);
    return 0;
}
```
The condition `1` is always true, so only `break` can end the loop. This avoids reading the first input outside the loop, as in Question 5.
:::

### 21. Skip and Stop (Optional)
**Question:** Print the numbers from `1` to `20`, each on its own line. Skip multiples of `3` with `continue`, and stop the loop completely with `break` once the number is greater than `12`.

**Expected Output:**
```text
1
2
4
5
7
8
10
11
```

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show answer"}
```c
#include <stdio.h>

int main() {
    for (int i = 1; i <= 20; i++) {
        if (i > 12) {
            break;
        }
        if (i % 3 == 0) {
            continue;
        }
        printf("%d\n", i);
    }
    return 0;
}
```
`12` is a multiple of `3`, so it is skipped. At `13`, the `break` ends the loop.
:::

### 22. Prime Check
**Question:** Read an integer `n` that is at least `2`. Print `Prime` if it has no divisor from `2` to `n - 1`, otherwise `Not prime`. Use a flag variable and stop the loop with `break` as soon as a divisor is found.

**Expected Program Output** (Input: 17)**:**
```text
Enter an integer (2 or more): 17
Prime
```

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show answer"}
```c
#include <stdio.h>

int main() {
    int n;
    int is_prime = 1;
    printf("Enter an integer (2 or more): ");
    scanf("%d", &n);
    printf("\n");

    for (int i = 2; i < n; i++) {
        if (n % i == 0) {
            is_prime = 0;
            break;
        }
    }

    if (is_prime) {
        printf("Prime\n");
    } else {
        printf("Not prime\n");
    }
    return 0;
}
```
The flag starts as "prime" and is set to `0` when a divisor is found. With input `18` the program prints `Not prime`, because `18 % 2 == 0` stops the loop at `i = 2`.
:::

### 23. Early Exit with `return`
**Question:** Read up to `5` integers. If the user enters `0` at any point, print `Zero entered, exiting.` and end the program immediately with `return 0;`. If all five numbers are read without a `0`, print `All numbers read.`

**Expected Program Output:**<br>
Input: 4, 7, 0
```text
Enter a number: 4
Enter a number: 7
Enter a number: 0
Zero entered, exiting.
```

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show answer"}
```c
#include <stdio.h>

int main() {
    int number;

    for (int i = 0; i < 5; i++) {
        printf("Enter a number: ");
        scanf("%d", &number);
        printf("\n");
        if (number == 0) {
            printf("Zero entered, exiting.\n");
            return 0;
        }
    }
    printf("All numbers read.\n");
    return 0;
}
```
With the input `1 2 3 4 5`, the program asks five times and then prints `All numbers read.`
:::

## Part 5 — Patterns and Number Problems

### 24. Fibonacci Sequence
**Question:** Read `N` from `1` to `45` and print the first `N` Fibonacci numbers on one line, separated by spaces, beginning with `0 1 1 2 3 ...`. Each number is the sum of the previous two. Use variables to remember the previous two numbers, not an array. For input outside `1` to `45`, print `Invalid input`.

**Expected Program Output** (Input: 8)**:**
```text
How many terms (1-45)? 8
0 1 1 2 3 5 8 13
```

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show answer"}
```c
#include <stdio.h>

int main() {
    int n;
    int a = 0, b = 1;
    printf("How many terms (1-45)? ");
    scanf("%d", &n);
    printf("\n");

    if (n < 1 || n > 45) {
        printf("Invalid input\n");
        return 0;
    }
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        printf("%d", a);
        if (i < n - 1) {
            printf(" ");
        }
        int next = a + b;
        a = b;
        b = next;
    }
    printf("\n");
    return 0;
}
```
`a` holds the number being printed and `b` the one after it. Each repetition computes `next`, then shifts both variables one step forward. The 46th Fibonacci number no longer fits in an `int`.
:::

### 25. Star Triangle (Optional)
**Question:** Use nested `for` loops to print this shape:

**Expected Output:**
```text

**
***
****
*****
```

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show answer"}

The outer loop counts rows. The inner loop prints as many stars as the current row number, and `printf("\n")` ends each row.

### 28. Sum of Digits
**Question:** Read a positive integer and print the sum of its digits. Use `% 10` to get the last digit and `/ 10` to remove it.

**Expected Program Output** (Input: 1234)**:**
```text
Enter a positive integer: 1234
Digit sum: 10
```

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show answer"}
```c
#include <stdio.h>

int main() {
    int n, sum = 0;
    printf("Enter a positive integer: ");
    scanf("%d", &n);
    printf("\n");

    while (n > 0) {
        sum += n % 10;
        n /= 10;
    }
    printf("Digit sum: %d\n", sum);
    return 0;
}
```
For `1234`, the loop adds `4`, `3`, `2`, and `1`.
:::

### 29. Greatest Common Divisor
**Question:** Read two positive integers and print their greatest common divisor (GCD) using Euclid's algorithm: while `b` is not `0`, replace `(a, b)` with `(b, a % b)`. The answer is the final `a`.

**Expected Program Output:**<br>
Input: 48 18
```text
Enter two positive integers: 48 18
GCD: 6
```

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show answer"}
```c
#include <stdio.h>

int main() {
    int a, b;
    printf("Enter two positive integers: ");
    scanf("%d %d", &a, &b);
    printf("\n");

    while (b != 0) {
        int temp = b;
        b = a % b;
        a = temp;
    }
    printf("GCD: %d\n", a);
    return 0;
}
```
Trace for `48 18`: `(48, 18)`, then `(18, 12)`, then `(12, 6)`, then `(6, 0)`. The loop stops and `a` is `6`.
:::

### 30. Fizz Buzz from 1 to N
**Question:** Read `N`. For every number from `1` to `N`, print `FizzBuzz` if it is divisible by both `3` and `5`, `Fizz` if divisible by `3`, `Buzz` if divisible by `5`, and otherwise the number. Print one item per line.

**Expected Program Output** (Input: 10)**:**
```text
Enter N: 10
1
2
Fizz
4
Buzz
Fizz
7
8
Fizz
Buzz
```

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show answer"}
```c
#include <stdio.h>

int main() {
    int n;
    printf("Enter N: ");
    scanf("%d", &n);
    printf("\n");

    for (int i = 1; i <= n; i++) {
        if (i % 3 == 0 && i % 5 == 0) {
            printf("FizzBuzz\n");
        } else if (i % 3 == 0) {
            printf("Fizz\n");
        } else if (i % 5 == 0) {
            printf("Buzz\n");
        } else {
            printf("%d\n", i);
        }
    }
    return 0;
}
```
This combines the loop with the `if` ladder from the Conditional Statements notebook.
:::

### 31. Power of a Number (Optional)
**Question:** Read an integer base and a non-negative integer exponent. Calculate `base` raised to `exponent` using a loop and multiplication only. Assume the result fits in an `int`.

**Expected Program Output:**<br>
Input: 2 10
```text
Enter base and exponent: 2 10
2^10 = 1024
```

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show answer"}
```c
#include <stdio.h>

int main() {
    int base, exponent;
    int result = 1;
    printf("Enter base and exponent: ");
    scanf("%d %d", &base, &exponent);
    printf("\n");

    for (int i = 0; i < exponent; i++) {
        result *= base;
    }
    printf("%d^%d = %d\n", base, exponent, result);
    return 0;
}
```
For an exponent of `0` the loop never runs, and the result stays `1`, which is correct.
:::

## Part 6 — Menus That Repeat

### 32. Calculator That Repeats
**Question:** Extend the calculator from the Conditional Statements notebook (`number operator number`, with `+`, `-`, `*`, `/`). After each result, ask `Calculate again? (y/n): `. If the user enters `y` or `Y`, calculate again. Any other answer ends the program with `Goodbye`. Keep the division-by-zero and unknown-operator messages.

**Expected Program Output:**<br>
Input: 8 / 2, y, 7 / 0, n
```text
Enter: number operator number: 8 / 2
Result: 4.00
Calculate again? (y/n): y
Enter: number operator number: 7 / 0
Cannot divide by zero
Calculate again? (y/n): n
Goodbye
```

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show answer"}
```c
#include <stdio.h>

int main() {
    char again = 'y';
    while (again == 'y' || again == 'Y') {
        double a, b;
        char op;
        printf("Enter: number operator number: ");
        scanf("%lf %c %lf", &a, &op, &b);
        printf("\n");

        if (op == '+') {
            printf("Result: %.2f\n", a + b);
        } else if (op == '-') {
            printf("Result: %.2f\n", a - b);
        } else if (op == '*') {
            printf("Result: %.2f\n", a * b);
        } else if (op == '/') {
            if (b == 0.0) {
                printf("Cannot divide by zero\n");
            } else {
                printf("Result: %.2f\n", a / b);
            }
        } else {
            printf("Unknown operator\n");
        }

        printf("Calculate again? (y/n): ");
        scanf(" %c", &again);
        printf("\n");
    }
    printf("Goodbye\n");
    return 0;
}
```
Starting `again` as `'y'` lets the loop run the first time. The space in `" %c"` skips the newline left over from the previous input.
:::

### 33. Repeating Unit Converter
**Question:** Repeat this menu until the user enters `0`. For choices `1` to `4`, read a value and print the result with two decimal places. For any other number, print `Invalid choice` and show the menu again. Print `Goodbye` when the user exits.

- `1` converts centimetres to metres
- `2` converts metres to centimetres
- `3` converts Celsius to Fahrenheit
- `4` converts Fahrenheit to Celsius
- `0` exits

**Expected Program Output:**<br>
Input: 1, 250, 0
```text
1: cm to m
2: m to cm
3: C to F
4: F to C
0: exit
Choice: 1
Enter value: 250
Result: 2.50 m
1: cm to m
2: m to cm
3: C to F
4: F to C
0: exit
Choice: 0
Goodbye
```

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show answer"}
```c
#include <stdio.h>

int main() {
    int choice = -1;
    while (choice != 0) {
        double value;
        printf("1: cm to m\n2: m to cm\n3: C to F\n4: F to C\n0: exit\nChoice: ");
        scanf("%d", &choice);
        printf("\n");

        if (choice == 0) {
            printf("Goodbye\n");
        } else if (choice >= 1 && choice <= 4) {
            printf("Enter value: ");
            scanf("%lf", &value);
            printf("\n");
            if (choice == 1) {
                printf("Result: %.2f m\n", value / 100.0);
            } else if (choice == 2) {
                printf("Result: %.2f cm\n", value * 100.0);
            } else if (choice == 3) {
                printf("Result: %.2f F\n", value * 9.0 / 5.0 + 32.0);
            } else {
                printf("Result: %.2f C\n", (value - 32.0) * 5.0 / 9.0);
            }
        } else {
            printf("Invalid choice\n");
        }
    }
    return 0;
}
```
`choice` starts at `-1` (any value except `0`) so the loop runs at least once.
:::

## Part 7 — Games with Loops

The games below use `rand()` from `<stdlib.h>` to let the computer choose randomly. Seed the generator **once**, at the start of `main`, with `srand((unsigned)time(NULL))` from `<time.h>`. Because the computer's choices are random, each example shows one possible run.

### 34. Random-Number Warm-Up (Optional)
**Question:** Seed the random-number generator once and choose a random integer from `0` to `2`. Print `Rock` for `0`, `Paper` for `1`, or `Scissors` for `2`.

**Expected Output** (one possible run)**:**
```text
Paper
```

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show answer"}
```c
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <time.h>

int main() {
    srand((unsigned)time(NULL));
    int choice = rand() % 3;

    if (choice == 0) {
        printf("Rock\n");
    } else if (choice == 1) {
        printf("Paper\n");
    } else {
        printf("Scissors\n");
    }
    return 0;
}
```
`rand() % 3` gives `0`, `1`, or `2`. The output changes from run to run.
:::

### 35. Guess the Number in Three Attempts
**Question:** The computer picks a secret number from `1` to `5`. The player has at most `3` guesses. If the player guesses correctly, print `You won!` and stop. If all `3` guesses are wrong, print `You lost! The number was X.`

**Expected Program Output:**<br>
Input: 2, 5, 4 (the secret number is `4`)
```text
Guess the number (1-5): 2
Guess the number (1-5): 5
Guess the number (1-5): 4
You won!
```

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show answer"}
```c
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <time.h>

int main() {
    srand((unsigned)time(NULL));
    int secret = rand() % 5 + 1;
    int guess;

    for (int i = 0; i < 3; i++) {
        printf("Guess the number (1-5): ");
        scanf("%d", &guess);
        printf("\n");

        if (guess == secret) {
            printf("You won!\n");
            return 0;
        }
    }

    printf("You lost! The number was %d.\n", secret);
    return 0;
}
```
The `for` loop allows at most three guesses. `return 0` ends the program immediately when the guess is correct; otherwise, the message after the loop is printed.
:::

### 36. Guess the Number (Second Version)
**Question:** The computer picks a secret number from `1` to `20`. The player has at most `5` guesses. After each wrong guess, print `Too low` or `Too high`. If the player guesses correctly, print `Correct! You won.` and stop. If all `5` guesses are used, print `Game over. The number was X.`

**Expected Program Output:**<br>
Input: 10, 15, 12 (the secret number is `12`)
```text
Guess 1 of 5: 10
Too low
Guess 2 of 5: 15
Too high
Guess 3 of 5: 12
Correct! You won.
```

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show answer"}
```c
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <time.h>

int main() {
    srand((unsigned)time(NULL));
    int secret = rand() % 20 + 1;
    int won = 0;

    for (int attempt = 1; attempt <= 5; attempt++) {
        int guess;
        printf("Guess %d of 5: ", attempt);
        scanf("%d", &guess);
        printf("\n");

        if (guess == secret) {
            printf("Correct! You won.\n");
            won = 1;
            break;
        } else if (guess < secret) {
            printf("Too low\n");
        } else {
            printf("Too high\n");
        }
    }

    if (!won) {
        printf("Game over. The number was %d.\n", secret);
    }
    return 0;
}
```
The `won` flag tells the code after the loop whether the loop ended by `break` or by running out of guesses. If the player misses all five guesses, the program prints `Game over. The number was 12.`
:::

### 37. Rock, Paper, Scissors: Play Again
**Question:** The player enters `r`, `p`, or `s`. The computer chooses randomly (`0` rock, `1` paper, `2` scissors). Print both choices and the result (`Draw`, `You win`, or `Computer wins`). Reject an invalid choice with `Invalid choice`. After every round, ask `Play again? (y/n): `. Repeat while the answer is `y` or `Y`, then print `Thanks for playing`.

**Expected Program Output:**<br>
Input: r, n<br>
Computer's Choice: Scissors
```text
Choose r (rock), p (paper), or s (scissors): r
You: Rock
Computer: Scissors
You win
Play again? (y/n): n
Thanks for playing
```

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show answer"}
```c
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <time.h>

int main() {
    char again = 'y';
    srand((unsigned)time(NULL));

    while (again == 'y' || again == 'Y') {
        char player;
        int computer = rand() % 3;  /* 0 rock, 1 paper, 2 scissors */
        printf("Choose r (rock), p (paper), or s (scissors): ");
        scanf(" %c", &player);
        printf("\n");

        if (player != 'r' && player != 'p' && player != 's') {
            printf("Invalid choice\n");
        } else {
            printf("You: ");
            if (player == 'r') printf("Rock\n");
            else if (player == 'p') printf("Paper\n");
            else printf("Scissors\n");

            printf("Computer: ");
            if (computer == 0) printf("Rock\n");
            else if (computer == 1) printf("Paper\n");
            else printf("Scissors\n");

            if ((player == 'r' && computer == 0) ||
                (player == 'p' && computer == 1) ||
                (player == 's' && computer == 2)) {
                printf("Draw\n");
            } else if ((player == 'r' && computer == 2) ||
                       (player == 'p' && computer == 0) ||
                       (player == 's' && computer == 1)) {
                printf("You win\n");
            } else {
                printf("Computer wins\n");
            }
        }

        printf("Play again? (y/n): ");
        scanf(" %c", &again);
        printf("\n");
    }
    printf("Thanks for playing\n");
    return 0;
}
```
Seed with `srand` once, outside the loop. Seeding inside the loop would repeat the same "random" number when rounds happen within the same second.
:::

### 38. Rock, Paper, Scissors: First to 3 Wins, Game Over After 5 Losses
**Question:** Extend the previous game into a match. Count the player's wins and losses. Draws and invalid choices count for neither side. After every round, print the score in the form `Wins: X | Losses: Y`. The match ends as soon as the player has `3` wins (print `You won the game!`) or `5` losses (print `Game over: you lost 5 rounds.`). Use a loop whose condition checks both counters.

**Expected Program Output:**<br>
Input: r, p, s, r, p<br>
Computer's Choices: Scissors, Scissors, Scissors, Scissors, Rock
```text
Choose r (rock), p (paper), or s (scissors): r
You: Rock
Computer: Scissors
You win this round
Wins: 1 | Losses: 0
Choose r (rock), p (paper), or s (scissors): p
You: Paper
Computer: Scissors
Computer wins this round
Wins: 1 | Losses: 1
Choose r (rock), p (paper), or s (scissors): s
You: Scissors
Computer: Scissors
Draw
Wins: 1 | Losses: 1
Choose r (rock), p (paper), or s (scissors): r
You: Rock
Computer: Scissors
You win this round
Wins: 2 | Losses: 1
Choose r (rock), p (paper), or s (scissors): p
You: Paper
Computer: Rock
You win this round
Wins: 3 | Losses: 1
You won the game!
```

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show answer"}
```c
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <time.h>

int main() {
    int wins = 0, losses = 0;
    srand((unsigned)time(NULL));

    while (wins < 3 && losses < 5) {
        char player;
        int computer = rand() % 3;  /* 0 rock, 1 paper, 2 scissors */

        printf("Choose r (rock), p (paper), or s (scissors): ");
        scanf(" %c", &player);
        printf("\n");

        if (player != 'r' && player != 'p' && player != 's') {
            printf("Invalid choice\n");
            continue;
        }

        printf("You: ");
        if (player == 'r') printf("Rock\n");
        else if (player == 'p') printf("Paper\n");
        else printf("Scissors\n");

        printf("Computer: ");
        if (computer == 0) printf("Rock\n");
        else if (computer == 1) printf("Paper\n");
        else printf("Scissors\n");

        if ((player == 'r' && computer == 0) ||
            (player == 'p' && computer == 1) ||
            (player == 's' && computer == 2)) {
            printf("Draw\n");
        } else if ((player == 'r' && computer == 2) ||
                   (player == 'p' && computer == 0) ||
                   (player == 's' && computer == 1)) {
            wins++;
            printf("You win this round\n");
        } else {
            losses++;
            printf("Computer wins this round\n");
        }
        printf("Wins: %d | Losses: %d\n", wins, losses);
    }

    if (wins == 3) {
        printf("You won the game!\n");
    } else {
        printf("Game over: you lost 5 rounds.\n");
    }
    return 0;
}
```
The condition `wins < 3 && losses < 5` keeps the match running only while both limits are still open. After the loop, exactly one of the two limits has been reached, so a single `if` decides the final message. For an invalid choice, `continue` skips the rest of the round and goes back to the loop condition without changing the score.
:::
